message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but the process is handled by the city’s police department and code‑enforcement offices rather than the city council itself. Here’s how to do it: | Step | What to do | Where to go / Who to call | |------|------------|---------------------------| | **1. Check the ordinance** | Atlanta’s Noise Ordinance (Title 10, Chapter 2 of the Atlanta Municipal Code) sets the limits for daytime and nighttime noise, defines “public nuisance,” and lists the penalties. It’s a good idea to review it first so you know what constitutes a violation.
**Link:** | | | **2. File a complaint online** | Use the city’s 311 portal to submit a noise complaint. You’ll need to provide the address, time of the disturbance, and a brief description. | **Website:** | | **3. Call 311 (non‑emergency)** | If you prefer to speak to someone, call 311 (404‑656‑3111). The operator will direct you to the appropriate department (usually the Atlanta Police Department’s Noise Enforcement Division). | **Phone:** 404‑656‑3111 | | **4. Contact the Atlanta Police Department (APD)** | For urgent or ongoing disturbances, you can call the APD’s non‑emergency line. They’ll dispatch an officer to investigate and, if necessary, issue a citation. | **Phone:** 404‑656‑3111 | | **5. Reach out to your city council member** | If you want to bring the issue to the council’s attention—perhaps because it’s a recurring problem or you’re seeking a broader policy change—contact your local council member’s office. They can raise the issue on the council floor or refer you to the appropriate committee. | **Find your council member:** | | **6. Follow up** | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy if you need to check the status or provide additional information. | | ### Quick Tips - **Timing matters:** Noise ordinances often have stricter limits after 10 p.m. and on Sundays. Make sure you note the exact time of the disturbance. - **Document evidence:** Photos, videos, or audio recordings can help the police assess the situation more accurately. - **Use the 311 app:** If you have a smartphone, the 311 app lets you submit complaints and track their status. ### Bottom Line While the city council creates and amends noise ordinances, the actual enforcement is carried out by the Atlanta Police Department and the city’s code‑enforcement teams. Filing a complaint through 311 or the APD’s non‑emergency line is the most direct way to get the issue addressed. If you want the council to consider a broader policy change, contact your council member after the complaint has been filed.
